newsitem.title: USA: Men's Wearhouse to buy C&R Clothiers assets.
newsitem.headline: Men's Wearhouse to buy C&R Clothiers assets.

text.p: Men's Wearhouse Inc said Wednesday agreed to acquire certain assets and leasehold interests of C&R Clothiers Inc, Los Angeles, which recently filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

Men's Wearhouse said that if the proposed acquisition were approved by the bankruptcy court, it would then launch a new division selling lower-priced men's apparel which would operate under the name C&R Clothiers.

Under the proposed deal, Men's Wearhouse said it would assume leases for up to 19 C&R stores in Southern California, enter into a lease for C&R's current distribution center in Culver City, Calif., and acquire its existing inventory and certain other assets.
The total cost of the transaction could be up to $13.5 million, the company said.
The new division would be headed by Neil Dinerman, who is currently president of C&R Clothiers.

"We believe that because this concept addresses a different and new market segment, it will have minimal impact on our core Men's Wearhouse business," said David Edwab, Men's Wearhouse's chief financial officer.
Edwab said the C&R Clothiers deal would not change the company's plans to open 45 to 50 Men's Wearhouse stores per year in fiscal 1996 and 1997.
Men's Wearhouse said it plans to roll out additional C&R units throughout the country in the near future.
